articles.title: 🎰 EU Orders Apps To Be Less Addictive; Users Refresh The Announcement 400 Times
articles.dateline: BRUSSELS — reported between two infinite scrolls
paras: Europe is moving to rein in what it calls "addictive design" at Meta — a bold plan to make apps less compelling that regulators announced, then checked their phones, then announced again.

"We want technology that respects your time," an official said, thumb hovering over a pull-to-refresh. Meta responded that its designs are merely "aggressively engaging," and that the little red notification dot is, if anything, a form of fine art.
Experts warn that a truly non-addictive app is technically just a calendar, and no human has downloaded one of those on purpose since 2004.

articles.title: 🐉 Chinese Lab Drops One Of The Biggest 'Open' A.I. Models; Download Is Merely 900 Gigabytes
articles.dateline: SHENZHEN-ISH — via a heroic USB stick
paras: A Chinese lab released one of the largest open frontier models yet — free for anyone to download, run, and immediately discover their laptop lacks the RAM, the patience, and the will to live required to do so.
"It's completely open," a researcher noted. "You just need a small datacenter and a forgiving electricity provider." The weights are so large that downloading them now counts, medically, as cardio.

articles.title: 🔵 Intel Rides A.I. Server Boom; Remembers, Fondly, That It Makes Chips
articles.dateline: SANTA CLARA — reported from a triumphant cubicle
paras: Intel is riding renewed demand for AI servers — a comeback so heartwarming analysts are calling it "the dad-rock of semiconductors": not flashy, been around forever, suddenly cool again at a wedding.
"We never left," Intel said, sweeping several difficult years under a rug of impressive size. Investors celebrated the news by remembering that the company exists.

articles.title: 🐱 Silicon Quantum Chips Move From Lab To Factory; Simultaneously Working And Not Working
paras: Silicon quantum computing projects are moving from lab to fab, meaning the qubits are now mass-produced and, per the laws of physics, both fully functional and completely broken until an accountant looks directly at the invoice.

"It's the future of computing," a physicist said, "assuming we can keep it colder than my ex's heart." The chips reportedly solve problems no one has yet, which is either revolutionary or a very expensive way to say "maybe."

articles.title: 💰 Memory Gold Rush Continues; Analysts Say Buy RAM, Hug It, Whisper To It
articles.dateline: SEOUL — filed from atop a pile of DIMMs
paras: With memory makers riding an AI-fueled boom, the industry has minted a fresh class of RAM millionaires — people who, a year ago, could not give a memory stick away at a garage sale.

"There has never been a better time to own something a computer desperately needs," an analyst said, gently cradling a DDR5 module like a newborn. Consumers, meanwhile, report their next upgrade now requires a co-signer.

Your quantum future is bright and also dim — simultaneously — until payday collapses the waveform.
Mercury enters the downloads folder. Estimated time remaining: 4 hours. Or never. Both.
